California Leaders Unveils Summer 2026 Magazine Featuring 17 Leaders Driving California's Future
data.description:
Statewide publication and August 10 launch at BMO Stadium spotlight the leaders advancing tourism, aviation, sports, business, innovation, and economic development across California.

LOS ANGELES, CA / ACCESS Newswire / August 7, 2026 / California Leaders today announced the release of its Summer 2026 issue, themed "California on the World Stage," featuring 17 influential leaders whose work is helping shape California's future through tourism, travel, aviation, sports, entertainment, business, law, innovation, and economic development.

The issue will be officially unveiled during the California Leaders Summer Issue Magazine Launch, Presented by BMO, on Monday, August 10, 2026, at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles, where more than 200 leaders from business, government, education, nonprofit organizations, and community organizations are expected to gather to celebrate leadership, collaboration, and California's continued global impact.

Following the successful FIFA World Cup 2026™, California is preparing to host Super Bowl LXI and the LA28 Olympic & Paralympic Games, creating unprecedented opportunities for tourism, workforce development, investment, innovation, and economic growth. The Summer 2026 issue highlights the leaders helping position California for this historic decade on the world stage.

"California's greatest strength has always been its people," said Christopher Luna, Publisher & CEO of California Leaders. "Our mission is to tell the stories of the leaders shaping California's future while creating opportunities for leaders across business, government, education, nonprofit, and community organizations to build relationships, share ideas, and work together. This issue celebrates the people whose leadership is strengthening California's economy, communities, and global competitiveness."

"Sharing this cover with Adam Burke is a genuine pleasure. Los Angeles and San Francisco are two front doors to the same state, and visitors who arrive in one city often find themselves exploring the other," said Anna Marie Presutti, President & CEO of the San Francisco Travel Association. "California is experiencing a once-in-a-generation run of global events-from this year's Super Bowl and FIFA World Cup matches in the Bay Area to Super Bowl LXI in Los Angeles and the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games. It's an opportunity we're better off celebrating together. The world isn't about to start watching California-it never stopped."

Presutti shares this issue's cover with Adam Burke, President & CEO of the Los Angeles Tourism & Convention Board, symbolizing the collaboration between California's two largest visitor destinations as the state prepares to welcome millions of visitors for the next generation of global sporting and cultural events.

  • Papia Gambelin - Managing Director, State & Local Government Affairs, United Airlines

  • Stephen Revetria - President, Giants Enterprises

  • Tammy Dickerson, CMP - CEO, The Baker Group

  • Teresa Guy, MBA - Vice President of Booking & Partnerships, Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum

  • Todd Johnson - President & CEO, Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce

Many of the featured leaders will participate in the magazine launch program, which will include keynote conversations, executive interviews, and discussions exploring California's future in tourism, sports, entertainment, workforce development, and economic competitiveness.

The evening's featured program includes:

  • Venue Host Remarks from John Thorrington, Co-President & General Manager, Los Angeles Football Club (LAFC)

  • Opening Remarks by Rachel Freeman, Deputy Mayor of Business & Economic Development, City of Los Angeles

  • Keynote Address by Doane Liu, Chief Tourism Officer, City of Los Angeles

  • Featured Fireside Conversation with Halé Behzadi, Vice Chair of BMO, and Stephen Revetria, President of Giants Enterprises

  • Women in Sports & Entertainment, moderated by Dr. Dayle M. Smith, Dean of the College of Business Administration at Loyola Marymount University, featuring Christy Castillo Butcher, Teresa Guy, Samona Caldwell, and Ginny Sze

  • Cover Leaders Conversation featuring Adam Burke and Anna Marie Presutti

The evening will conclude with the official unveiling of the Summer 2026 issue of California Leaders Magazine, followed by a networking reception bringing together leaders from across California to strengthen relationships and foster collaboration across sectors.

data.title: GEORGE RISK INDUSTRIES, INC. FY 2026: Revenue $24.85M, EPS $2.32— 10-K Summary
data.description:
GEORGE RISK INDUSTRIES, INC. reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $24.85M and net income of $11.39M, with diluted earnings per share of $2.32, driven by higher sales and a material gain from marketable securities that boosted investment income versus the prior year.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $24.85M, compared with $22.54M in the prior year; YoY change 10.3%.
  • Net income was $11.39M, compared with $7.13M in the prior year; YoY change 59.7%.
  • Diluted EPS was $2.32, compared with $1.45 in the prior year; YoY change 60%.

Business Highlights

  • Revenue growth: Net sales rose 10.3% to $24.85M, reflecting price increases and stronger demand.
  • Channel & market mix: Sales are primarily through distributors to security installers; international sales represented about 9.6% of revenue.
  • Product and brand momentum: The company emphasized its American-made positioning and customer service while expanding engineering efforts into wireless and high-security product lines.
  • Operations: Inventory and prepayments increased to support higher sales; production reconfiguration and automation projects are underway to improve throughput.
  • Investment income impact: Gains on marketable securities materially boosted earnings and support reinvestment and potential acquisition flexibility.

Original SEC Filing: GEORGE RISK INDUSTRIES, INC. [ RSKIA ] - 10-K - Aug. 07, 2026

Princeton Bancorp, Inc. Q2 2026: Revenue $31.66M, Net income $7.08M, EPS $1.04— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Princeton Bancorp, Inc. reported second-quarter 2026 results driven by a rebound in profitability: revenue (interest & dividend income) totaled $31.656M, net income was $7.081M and diluted EPS came in at $1.04, versus $32.756M, $0.688M and $0.1, respectively, in the year‑ago quarter.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $31.656M, down from $32.756M in Q2 2025 (3.4%).
  • Net income was $7.081M, up from $0.688M in Q2 2025 (up $6.393M YoY).
  • Diluted EPS was $1.04, versus $0.10 in Q2 2025 (up $0.94 YoY).

Business Highlights

  • Net income recovery: Strong operational profit rebound with Q2 net income of $7.1M and H1 $13.3M, supported by lower credit provisions and higher net interest income.
  • Loan portfolio shift: Overall loans declined modestly as reductions in CRE and construction lending were offset by growth in home equity and residential mortgages.
  • Deposit and funding mix: Customers moved from CDs into money market and non‑interest checking accounts, bolstering on‑balance liquidity and funding flexibility.
  • Credit quality and risk management: Non‑performing assets remained stable at about 0.92% of loans with consistent allowance coverage and active ALCO oversight of interest rate risk.
  • Liquidity and market positioning: The company increased investment securities and maintained available borrowing lines (FHLB, discount window, ACBB) to preserve liquidity amid rate uncertainty.

Original SEC Filing: Princeton Bancorp, Inc. [ BPRN ] - 10-Q - Aug. 07, 2026

Europe's Hospitals on Red Alert as Four Countries Enter the Critical Cyber-Risk Tier
data.description:
Black Book Research's Europe-30 Healthcare Cyber Risk Pressure Index places Poland, the United Kingdom, France and Germany in the highest-pressure band as ransomware, supplier concentration and prolonged recovery threaten care delivery through 2027

CITY OF LONDON, GB / ACCESS Newswire / August 7, 2026 / Black Book Research has released Europe's Healthcare Cybersecurity Hotspots 2026, an independent assessment of cybersecurity pressure across hospitals, health systems and public health agencies in 30 European countries.

The European index identifies Poland, the United Kingdom, France and Germany in the critical risk-pressure tier, with nine additional countries classified as very high risk. The index measures the combined pressure created by current attacks, clinical digital dependence, supplier concentration, health-system scale, geopolitical exposure and recovery friction. It does not rank national competence or predict whether a specific hospital will be breached.

Four Countries Define Europe's Critical Tier

Poland

Poland ranks first as repeated hospital attacks converge with national-scale digital dependence and exceptional geopolitical pressure. Cyberattacks against hospitals in Krakow and Szczecin required national response support, disrupted systems and, in the Szczecin case, prompted prosecutors to examine potential danger to patient life and health. The country's expanding digital health infrastructure improves access but also raises the consequences of identity failure, shared-service compromise and synchronized regional disruption.

United Kingdom

The United Kingdom ranks second because NHS scale can turn a supplier or identity compromise into a multi-organization care-delivery event. National digital services, integrated care systems and extensive dependence on diagnostic, pathology and technology suppliers create concentrated exposure across scheduling, laboratory operations, referrals and clinical workflows. Recovery maturity is improving, but capability remains uneven across a healthcare estate comprising thousands of organizations and interconnected service providers.

France

France ranks third after severe multi-site disruption demonstrated how long hospital recovery can take. The October 2025 attack on CHI Haute-Comté affected Pontarlier and seven associated sites. By March 2026, more than 1,000 workstations and approximately 200 applications remained in the rebuild, with full normalization not expected before early 2027. France's scale, shared applications and regional interdependence make recovery sequencing as consequential as initial containment.

Germany

Germany ranks fourth with Europe's largest hospital attack surface, a highly distributed provider environment and extensive medical-device and supplier exposure. Germany reported 759 hospital beds per 100,000 people in 2024, while incidents involving AMEOS and Unimed demonstrated how external service providers can aggregate risk across otherwise independent hospitals. Reporting linked the Unimed incident to more than 135,000 affected people across connected institutions.

Together, the four countries illustrate different paths to critical risk: repeated attacks and geopolitical exposure in Poland, national scale and supplier concentration in the United Kingdom, prolonged multi-site recovery in France, and exceptional system complexity in Germany.

"Across the EU and its connected European healthcare markets, the most consequential threat is no longer a standalone ransomware payload. It is the convergence of identity compromise, session and token theft, exploitation of internet-facing edge systems, privileged supplier access and concentrated cross-border platforms, conditions that can convert one intrusion into a multi-hospital clinical-continuity event, said Doug Brown, Founder of Black Book.

Black Book's Europe-30 analysis identifies where NIS2 accountability, EHDS expansion, hybrid-threat exposure and recovery friction intersect, and where hospitals must be able to re-establish trusted identity, isolate supplier connections, rebuild clean endpoints and validate care pathways before patient safety is affected."

Key Findings

Thirteen of the 30 European countries assessed fall within the index's two highest pressure bands: Poland, the United Kingdom, France and Germany are classified as Critical, while Belgium, the Netherlands, Romania, Spain, Italy, Ireland, Switzerland, Lithuania and Norway are classified as Very High.

  • Ransomware remains the dominant threat, but identity compromise and concentrated suppliers are expanding the operational blast radius.

  • A single laboratory, EHR provider, cloud platform or managed-service supplier can expose multiple hospitals through shared infrastructure and trusted access.

  • Recovery must be measured through restored clinical workflows-not server availability or backup completion alone.

  • Hospital boards should prioritize phishing-resistant identity controls, supplier isolation, clean-room recovery and tested clinical downtime procedures.

The report applies six weighted dimensions and includes 19 documented 2025-2026 incidents and enforcement events, 33 threat-actor and malware profiles, an 18-domain hospital resilience framework and a vendor-agnostic directory of 50 cybersecurity software and services providers active in Europe.

Europe's Healthcare Cybersecurity Hotspots 2026: The Black Book Research Europe-30 Risk Pressure Index for Hospitals, Health Systems and Public Health Agencies is available for registration and download through the Black Book Research Reports Library at blackbookmarketresearch.com or register directly at https://blackbookmarketresearch.com/europe-hospital-cyber-exposure-and-clinical-continuity-index-2026
